evidence: harmonised definitions for numerical-uncalibrated simulation; thresholds marked ASSUMED are engineering judgements to be falsified by user tests
aggregation: A metric passes if the nominal scenario passes; the design envelope (short turns, 18 m/s, gust/crosswind, moguls) is reported as stress; faults (snag, power loss, component failure) are judged only on safety metrics (bodyForcePeak, keMax) and on graceful loss of footage. A concept passes overall only if every gating metric passes on nominal and no safety metric fails in any scenario.

sources.faa107: FAA 14 CFR Part 107 Subpart D (operations over people): Cat 1 ≤0.55 lb (250 g) and no exposed rotating parts that would lacerate skin; Cat 2 transfer ≤11 ft·lbf (14.9 J) on impact — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/subpart-D
sources.eu945: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/945, Annex Part 1–2 (class C0 <250 g; class C1 <900 g or transfer <80 J to a human head) — https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg_del/2019/945/oj
sources.eu947: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/947, UAS.OPEN.020/060 (A1 over uninvolved people for C0; VLOS except follow-me mode) — https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2019/947/oj
sources.astm3389: ASTM F3389/F3389M Standard Test Method for Assessing the Safety of Small Unmanned Aircraft Impacts (transferred-energy test used as an FAA means of compliance)
sources.assure: ASSURE A4 UAS Ground Collision Severity Evaluation (FAA, 2017): blunt-trauma risk of small UAS depends on transferred energy and structural compliance, KE alone overestimates harm of flexible <250 g airframes
sources.deleva: de Leva P. (1996) Adjustments to Zatsiorsky–Seluyanov segment inertia parameters, J Biomech 29(9):1223–1230 (whole-body centroidal inertias ≈ 1–1.5 kg·m² longitudinal, ≈ 11–15 kg·m² antero-posterior/medio-lateral for an adult)
sources.leishman: Leishman J.G., Principles of Helicopter Aerodynamics, 2nd ed., ch. 2 (momentum theory, Glauert forward-flight inflow, figure of merit)
sources.iec62368: IEC 62368-1: ES1 (touch-safe) limit 60 V DC under normal conditions; above it reinforced insulation/safeguards are required
sources.liion: Li-ion cell datasheets (e.g. Samsung INR21700, Molicel P-series): charge temperature 0–45 °C with reduced current (typ. ≤0.3–0.5 C) below ~10 °C to avoid lithium plating
sources.djigimbal: DJI consumer gimbal drones specify angular vibration range ±0.01° (e.g. Mini 4 Pro / Air 3 spec sheets): residual rate ≪1 °/s
sources.sim: Shared skier model sim/js/concepts/common/skier.js: m 80 kg, CdA 0.5 m², ρ 1.0 ⇒ aerodynamic drag 36 N at 12 m/s, 81 N at 18 m/s
sources.airbag: Avalanche airbag backpacks typically 2.3–3.2 kg (manufacturer data, e.g. Mammut/Scott/Black Diamond 2023–2025 ranges)

avail.definition: Percentage of SKIING time (rider speed > 2 m/s and not fallen, inside the intended filming window) during which the delivered output frame contains the full body (feet, head, shoulders, ski tips) with subject height ≥ 300 px in a 1920×1080-equivalent output, resolution limited by native sensor pixels (no upscaling credit), and no product artefact (tether, boom) ≥ 1 px wide crossing the subject silhouette unless the product removes it (e.g. declared inpainting).
avail.rationale: User goal "continuous" footage of a run; 80 % keeps ≥ 2.4 min of a 3-min run usable. Stopped / launch / dock / deploy time is excluded from the denominator because the rider is not skiing; post-fall time is excluded because there is nothing to film that the user wants scored, but footage lost while still skiing after a fault (snag → retract, drone lost) counts against the product.

deviations.boom360: Threshold ≥70 %; denominator is the whole scenario (index.js l.149–150) including standstill, deploy and post-fall time, so falls show 49.9 % although the boom films 100 % of the skiing time. No artefact rule needed (boom hidden in the stitch slab; subject sits on the seam — seamParallax informational).
deviations.trackdrone: Threshold ≥80 % OK; denominator = drone FILMING modes incl. lost/hold (index.js l.150/164) rather than skiing time — values almost identical in audit (≤0.2 pp).
deviations.tetherdrone: Threshold ≥80 % OK; denominator = all samples after 2 s settle incl. stopped/fallen time (index.js l.110/117). Tether-over-subject artefact is a separate metric (tetherCross 100 %, visible ≥0.5 px 93–100 %) and is NOT folded into avail: under the harmonised rule avail drops to ≈0 % unless tether inpainting is credited.

pxMed.definition: Median subject height (feet→head) in output px of a 1080p-equivalent frame, native-resolution limited, over skiing samples in which the subject is in frame.
pxMed.rationale: 300 px ≈ 28 % of frame height = a full/long shot in which body posture and ski technique are legible; consistent across concepts already.

deviations.boom360: consistent (min of 5.7K angular resolution and crop fill)
deviations.tetherdrone: consistent (≤2× crop of 4K); computed over flying samples incl. stopped rider

jitterRms.definition: RMS over skiing+filming samples of the >1 Hz component (zero-phase 2nd-order Butterworth high-pass at 1 Hz, contiguous ≥2 s segments, 0.5 s edges dropped) of the INERTIAL angular rate of the camera→subject-mid line of sight, combined in quadrature with the residual (un-stabilised) camera rotation rate of the delivered frame. Rationale for the LOS form: a gimbal, EIS or 360 subject-lock reframe removes camera rotation and slow drift but cannot remove high-frequency LOS motion caused by relative translation — it can only show it as subject shake or as background shake.
jitterRms.rationale: At 1080p with ~55–75° VFOV (14–20 px/°), 3 °/s RMS of >1 Hz motion ≈ 0.1° RMS at ~5 Hz ≈ 1.5–2 px displacement: the boundary between gimbal-like and visibly shaky. Consumer gimbals reach ≪1 °/s (±0.01° spec); hand-held/body-locked footage is 10–30 °/s. Low-pass content (deliberate reframing, turn-rate drift) is excluded because subject-tracking crops remove it and viewers accept it as camera work. ASSUMED engineering threshold; falsification test: paired-comparison viewer study at 2/3/5 °/s.

deviations.boom360: Uses subject-in-crop rate after a ASSUMED τ=0.15 s two-pass zero-phase tracking crop (model.js l.1059–1070) plus EIS residual, no high-pass, threshold 5 °/s, and a secondary jitterBoom ≤3 °/s. Audit LOS form: nominal 6.7, short 18.8, moguls 34 °/s (in-crop 1 Hz HP 5.8 / 13.3 / 29.8) — fail in every moving scenario.
deviations.trackdrone: Uses the shared losJitter() (|Δ∠LOS| − |Δ∠fwd|, env.js l.102–108: a magnitude difference that underestimates the vector rate by ≈25 %) with no high-pass, threshold 5 °/s, and a residual-gimbal model whose ANGLE noise scales with the airframe tilt RATE (model.js l.784–786), adding ≈4 °/s of artificial rate. Audit: 4.4 °/s with that residual, 1.8 °/s with a rate-consistent 0.2 % leak + 0.5 °/s floor (nominal); short turns 7.5–9.6 °/s.
deviations.tetherdrone: Own scalar magnitude difference (index.js l.119–127), no residual stabilisation term, no high-pass, threshold <5 °/s. Audit: 0.8 °/s nominal, 0.9 short turns, 2.2 power fault, 9.1 snag.

azRange.definition: Span (p5–p95) of viewing azimuth relative to the rider heading that the product can DELIVER ON COMMAND within one run, measured on the 0.2 Hz low-passed azimuth (turn-induced wobble is not shot variety).
azRange.rationale: Brief asks for rear/side/front reachability; a rear-only follow shot is a valid minimum product, so this metric is scored but not a kill criterion.

deviations.boom360: Reported informational; the 25–71° spans are counter-rotation wobble of a body-locked rear view (deliberate span ≈ 0°).
deviations.trackdrone: ≥45° gating; nominal 22° fails because no side pass is commanded in that scenario although a side mode exists (scenario choice, not capability).
deviations.tetherdrone: Not judged; 57–124° spans include turn wobble; side station (az 70°) demonstrated in scenario side.

addedMass.definition: Total mass worn on the body while skiing, including docked aircraft, pack batteries/power banks the concept relies on, reels, mounts and frames (excluding a backpack the rider would carry anyway).
addedMass.rationale: ≈2 % of body mass; half an avalanche-airbag pack (2.3–3.2 kg, which freeriders accept for a safety function). Mass far from the body is penalised separately through added inertia.

deviations.boom360: Threshold ≤2.0 kg (1.16 kg passes either way). Companion inertia metrics use a wrong roll reference (centroidal 12.5 kg·m² vs added inertia about the feet; consistent reference ≈85–93 kg·m² ⇒ 3.9 % not 26 %).
deviations.trackdrone: Pass hard-coded true; 0.395 kg omits the pack power bank that POD_CHARGE_W (index.js l.13) relies on (≈0.3–0.5 kg for 50–75 Wh).
deviations.tetherdrone: 1.2 kg hard-coded (ASSUMED breakdown), threshold <1.5 kg, consistent.

bodyForcePeak.definition: Peak 50 ms moving mean of |device force on the body| minus the static weight of the worn parts, over all scenarios in which the rider is upright (normal skiing and faults such as snags); fall impacts are judged by a separate fall-load check (root moment / weak link).
bodyForcePeak.rationale: ≈5 % of body weight and comparable to the skier’s own aerodynamic drag at 12 m/s (36 N) and to gust loads, which skiers absorb routinely; a larger transient pull at the back is a plausible fall trigger. ASSUMED engineering threshold.

deviations.boom360: Threshold 150 N, instantaneous 1–4 ms peak including static weight 11.4 N (model.js l.432). Audit: nominal 6 N, gust 18 N, snag 101 N (fail) — and the snag value is set by the scenario’s ASSUMED branch slip load of 200 N (index.js l.72) because the fold fuse limits bending moment only, not axial pull.
deviations.trackdrone: Threshold 10 N; computed as worn mass × horizontal skier acceleration only (index.js l.195–196). ~1 N: pass under any definition.
deviations.tetherdrone: Threshold 15 N (weak link), 20 ms mean tether tension, excludes worn weight; 1.8–5.8 N: pass.

handsBusy.definition: Percentage of skiing time during which a hand must operate the device (1 s per action while moving; actions while stopped do not count).
handsBusy.rationale: Poles must stay usable; actions at stops are covered by ops/setupTime.

deviations.tetherdrone: counts one 1 s tap per run against the scenario duration even when stopped (index.js l.181): 3–5 %; harmonised 0 %

setupTime.definition: Seconds of user standstill attributable to the device per run (deploy/launch to filming-ready + stow/dock to lift-ready), at the 90th percentile over a 0–9 m/s wind sweep, including fallback recovery (e.g. manual pick-up after failed docking).
setupTime.rationale: ≈5 % of a 10-min lift cycle and comparable to the time riders already spend at the top (goggles, bindings).

deviations.boom360: ≤60 s; 6.35 s computed from deploy/retract rates (+2 s): pass under any definition.
deviations.trackdrone: ≤25 s at 0.6× the scenario wind only (index.js l.188); dock success 67 % at 6 m/s and 0 % at 9 m/s ⇒ p90 includes manual retrieval (≈+20–30 s) ⇒ fragile.
deviations.tetherdrone: ≤60 s; nominal uses a fixed estimate SETUP_EST 14.15 s; dock scenario 15.1 s at 3 m/s gusty only; higher winds untested.

ops.definition: User actions per run (deploy/launch, stow/land, battery swap, recovery).
ops.rationale: One action to start, at most one to finish.

keMax.definition: Max of ½·m_eff·|v_device − v_ref|² where v_ref is the velocity of the person the device can strike WITHOUT the rider being in the same collision: ground frame (stationary bystander) for any part > 1.5 m from the rider’s body; rider frame for parts within the rider’s own 1.5 m envelope (a bystander struck there is struck by an 80 kg rider carrying ≥5.8 kJ, which the product does not add). m_eff = whole airframe for drones; tip camera + ⅓ of the boom for a compliant boom.
keMax.rationale: 11 ft·lbf FAA Cat 2 transferred-energy limit for flight over people (skiers below the flight path are uninvolved people). 80 J (EU C1 head-transfer limit) is retained only as a hard kill line. Note the regulatory alternative: FAA Cat 1 and EU C0 allow ≤250 g aircraft without exposed rotating parts over people with no energy limit, so a fail here is a physics-harm flag, not automatically a legal bar; an ASTM F3389 transfer test of a crushable shroud could also satisfy 14.9 J at higher KE.

deviations.boom360: Threshold 80 J and KE of the whole chain relative to the SNOW (index.js l.223): 50 J nominal, 102 J at 18 m/s (fail) — dominated by the rider’s own speed. Harmonised (rider frame): 0.3 J nominal, ≤5.9 J in falls: pass. Camera-only ground-frame KE is 18 J nominal — the verdict is definition-dependent.
deviations.trackdrone: Ground frame, 14.9 J: consistent. 24.4 J nominal (needs ≤150 g at 14 m/s).
deviations.tetherdrone: keMax ground frame 14.9 J: consistent (19.7 J nominal, fail). keRelNear (rider-relative at closest approach, 0.03 J) must not be read as a bystander pass because the drone is 5 m from the rider.

endurance.definition: Cumulative minutes of filming per charge of everything worn, at −10 °C, keeping the concept’s reserve, at the nominal-scenario mean power.
endurance.rationale: A ski day has ~15–20 runs of ~3 min ≈ 45–60 min of filmable skiing; a product that films only one run per charge is not "convenient". Recharging is credited only if physically feasible (cold-charge C-rate, carried power bank mass counted).

deviations.boom360: Hard-coded 75 min ASSUMED (index.js l.224), ≥60 min; plausible for a 360 camera in the cold, deploy motor energy ignored.
deviations.trackdrone: Per-RUN criterion ≥4 min (index.js l.215): 6.3 min passes; product-level 4.5 min per battery at 96 W mean (cold usable 7.2 Wh) ⇒ 7–10 batteries for 45 min; pod recharge 20 W into 5 °C cells ≈1.5 C exceeds cold-charge limits ⇒ fail.
deviations.tetherdrone: ≥45 min from a 100 Wh pack: 141 min nominal; consistent.

proposedAdditional.addedInertia: Added yaw inertia ≤25 % of body+skis yaw inertia (≈2.5 kg·m²) and added roll inertia about the feet ≤10 % of ≈90 kg·m²; boom360 0.60 kg·m² yaw (24 %) and 3.27 kg·m² roll (3.6–4 %) both pass when the reference is consistent.
proposedAdditional.artefactInFrame: Folded into avail (≥1 px device artefact on the subject).
proposedAdditional.electricalSafety: Any conductor on or near the body ≤60 V DC (ES1) or reinforced insulation + ground-fault cut-off; tetherdrone 100 V bus needs the latter.
